topics.label: Lecture Introduction
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture by introducing its overarching focus on the initiation and resolution of inflammation.

topics.label: Pathogen and Damage Recognition Signals
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the molecular signals used by the innate immune system to recognize pathogens, detect tissue damage, and distinguish self from non-self.

topics.label: Pattern Recognition Receptors and Intracellular Signaling
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the receptors and intracellular pathways responsible for detecting danger signals and transducing pro-inflammatory cascades.

topics.label: Inflammatory Mediators, Leukocyte Recruitment, and Systemic Consequences
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how acute immune activation coordinates cellular trafficking and produces localized as well as systemic physiological responses.

topics.label: Resolution of Inflammation, Tissue Repair, and Chronic Containment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the body terminates acute inflammation, rebuilds tissue integrity, and contains unresolvable insults through chronic inflammatory structures.

topics.label: Lecture Closing
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture and previews the next session on the complement system.
